lines.content: description: Apply the SE-EDU Git commit-message conventions to commits in this project.
For every commit in this repository:
- Write a clear subject in imperative mood, capitalize its first letter, omit the final period, and keep it at most 72 characters (prefer 50).
- Use an optional concise scope or category when useful.
- Give non-trivial commits a body separated from the subject by a blank line, wrapping body lines at 72 characters.
- Explain what changed and why; do not describe implementation steps that the diff already shows.
description: Apply the SE-EDU basic and intermediate Java coding conventions to this project.
Apply these conventions to Java code in this repository:
- Use lowercase package names, PascalCase class and enum names, camelCase variables and methods, and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants.
- Use four spaces for indentation, K&R braces, consistent imports, and a hard line limit of 120 characters.
- Initialize variables at declaration when practical and keep them in the smallest useful scope.
- Use braces for every loop and conditional body, including single-statement bodies.
- Keep logical blocks separated by blank lines and write comments in English using American spelling.
- Add descriptive JavaDoc header comments to all classes and public methods, except getters/setters and overriding methods whose inherited documentation applies exactly.
- Keep JavaDoc summaries concise and begin method summaries with a verb such as `Returns`, `Adds`, or `Creates`.

This repository is a starter template for a greenfield Java project used in an introductory software engineering course in an undergraduate computer science program. Students use it as the starting point for their own projects.

Unless the user says otherwise, assume that you are assisting a student working on a project in this repository. If the user identifies themselves as an instructor or another project stakeholder, adapt your response to that role.
* Prior knowledge: Basic Java and OOP concepts.
* IDE and level of expertise: Intermediate experience with using IntelliJ
* Explain the rationale for significant actions: what you did and why.
* Keep explanations brief but instructive, supporting learning through responsible use of AI. For example:
* When suggesting a Git command, briefly explain what it does.
* Add explanatory Javadoc comments to all classes and to nontrivial methods and fields when their purpose or behavior is not obvious.
* Make generated code as self-explanatory as possible, and include explanatory comments where they improve understanding.
* When faced with a design choice, choose the simplest option that is sufficient for the requirements, while briefly explaining relevant more advanced alternatives.
JUnit tests should focus on approximately the highest-value 50% of methods, prioritizing
complex, core, or critical business logic. Update the relevant JUnit tests after every
code change so that the project continues to meet this coverage target.
Ensure that Java 25 is used when running the application or build tasks. On macOS, use `sdk use java 25.0.3.fx-zulu` to switch to Java 25 if needed.
Use lightweight tags unless the user requests an annotated tag.
When proposing or creating a commit message, include enough detail to explain the rationale for the change.
Do not commit or push unless explicitly asked.
This is a project template for a greenfield Java project. Given below are instructions on how to use it.
Prerequisites: JDK 25, update Intellij to the most recent version.
1. Open Intellij (if you are not in the welcome screen, click `File` > `Close Project` to close the existing project first)
1. Open the project into Intellij as follows:
1. Select the project directory, and click `OK`.
1. If there are any further prompts, accept the defaults.
1. Configure the project to use **JDK 25** (not other versions) as explained in [here](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/sdk.html#set-up-jdk).
In the same dialog, set the **Project language level** field to the `SDK default` option.

1. After that, locate the `src/main/java/Nexus.java` file, right-click it, and choose `Run Nexus.main()` (if the code editor is showing compile errors, try restarting the IDE). If the setup is correct, you should see the chatbot greeting and farewell as the output:
What can I do for you?
Bye. Hope to see you again soon!

**Warning:** Keep the `src\main\java` folder as the root folder for Java files (i.e., don't rename those folders or move Java files to another folder outside of this folder path), as this is the default location some tools (e.g., Gradle) expect to find Java files.
